reports.title: Best Buy Reports Third Quarter Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 5.8% to $10.24bn and adjusted EPS of $1.62, both above estimates; comps +6.1%; FY27 outlook raised
results: Revenue rose 5.8% to $10.24bn, above the $9.91bn estimate; adjusted EPS of $1.62 (+16%) beat the $1.49 estimate.
Comparable sales grew 6.1%, the best in five years, led by computing, phones and newer lines such as AI glasses and trading cards.
US gross margin improved to 24.1%, helped by $41m of tariff refunds and growth in Marketplace and ads, partly offset by lower product margins.
Higher incentive pay and spending on Marketplace and ads pushed the US adjusted cost ratio up to 19.6% of revenue.
Best Buy returned $350m in the quarter ($201m dividends, $149m buybacks) and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.96 a share.

guidance.summary: Full-year FY27 targets were raised: revenue of $43.0–43.3bn and adjusted EPS of $6.90–7.05, with the EPS range above consensus. Q4 comparable sales are guided to +2% to +4%.

points: Computing demand held up even though average prices rose about 25% on memory costs and a shift to premium machines; unit sales fell.
Management said it has enough computing stock for the holidays, having bought some inventory early, but would not say when memory supply eases.
No tariff-refund help is expected in Q4, and next year will lap about $75m of refunds.
Marketplace sales are expected to pass $1.3bn this year, and the ads business is on track for about 10% growth.
Holiday promotions look similar to last year; management said it is still very early in the quarter.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 24 Nov 2026; StockAnalysis, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Holiday-quarter comparable sales against the +2% to +4% guide in a competitive season.
Memory costs and computing unit volumes as higher prices persist.
Margins without tariff refunds, with rising incentive pay feeding into next year's costs.
